title: Ontological Commitment Detection Schema
description: Structured results of ontological commitment detection in philosophical arguments. Identifies the entities a theory or argument is committed to, categorized by entity type and explicitness.

analysis_id.description: Unique identifier for this ontological commitment analysis run

source_argument_id.description: Identifier of the source argument or text under analysis

entity_type.description: The kind of entity the argument commits to (e.g., 'electron', 'moral property', 'possible world')

category.description: Ontological category of the committed entity

explicitness.description: How explicitly the commitment appears in the text

source_location.description: Textual location or quotation indicating the commitment

quinean_test.description: Result of applying Quine's criterion of ontological commitment (bound variable analysis)

controversiality.description: Degree of controversy surrounding this ontological commitment

alternative_paraphrase.description: Potential paraphrase that avoids or reduces this commitment

rejection_impact.description: Impact on the argument if this commitment is rejected

ontological_profile.description: Aggregate profile of the argument's ontological commitments

quinean_ontology.description: Overall ontological verdict based on Quinean criterion — what the argument says there is

most_contentious_commitment.description: The single most controversial ontological commitment identified

category_summary.description: Count of commitments per ontological category
